Choose each delimiter and each script by what it says, so a reader can tell the argument of a [function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-function) from a group of [term](defining-terms.qmd#def-term)s, and an index from a power.

Delimiters:

- Parentheses group terms and hold the argument of a function: $\pf{x}$, $\Var{X}$, $\Prf{A}$, and $(a, b)$ for an open interval.
- Square brackets hold the argument of an [expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation), $\E{X}$, and the closed end of an interval, $[a, b]$.
- Curly braces hold the members of a set, $\set{x : x > 0}$, and an event inside an indicator.
- Write no more than two levels of one kind of delimiter.
  Past that, change the kind or name the sub-expression with a macro.

Scripts:

- A subscript says which one.
  It is an index, as in $x_i$, or it names the random variable or variable that a quantity belongs to, as in $\mu_X$ and $\tau_X$.
  Drop it when only one is in play.
- A superscript is a power, as in $x^2$.
  Wrap an iteration or sample index in parentheses, as in $\vx^{(t)}$, so that it is not mistaken for an exponent.
- Write a transpose or an inverse through its macro, `\tp{}` or `\inv{}`, not as a typed $\top$ or $-1$.
- Do not put a subscript on a subscript, or a superscript on a superscript.
  Name the sub-expression with a macro instead.

Give the characteristic of a random variable a subscript when it has its own symbol, as in $\tau_X$, and keep the argument when it is an operator, as in $\Var{X}$.
A letter followed by a parenthesis, such as $\tau(X)$, reads as a function applied to $X$, and so as a new random variable.

::: {#exm-delimiters-and-scripts}

## A characteristic with its own symbol

> ❌ The precision of $X$ is $\tau(X) = 1 / \operatorname{Var}[X]$.
>
> ✅ The precision of $X$ is $\tau_X = 1 / \Var{X}$.

The ✅ version writes the precision as a number with the random variable as a subscript, and writes the [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance) with its parenthesized argument.

:::
